title: Gentle Work at the Base of the Skull
summary: The finger pads make gentle contact with the muscular tissues just below the occipital bone, without pressing on bone or the front of the neck.
goal: Work delicately around the small suboccipital area using minimal pressure.
imageAlt: Educational diagram of gentle contact with muscles at the base of the skull.
startingPosition: The head is fully supported and remains neutral. The fingers rest just below the occipital bone at the back of the head.
instructions: Locate the soft tissues immediately below the occipital bone.
Place the finger pads symmetrically on either side of the midline.
Hold for a few seconds without digging in.
Release smoothly and move to a nearby small area.
direction: Small local contacts below the occipital bone on either side of the midline.
areasText: muscles at the base of the skull
mistakes: Pressing directly onto the occipital bone.
Extending or rotating the head while applying pressure.
warning: Avoid this technique after recent head or neck injury, with marked dizziness, neurological symptoms, or unexplained severe headache. Do not press on the front or side of the neck.
telegramCaption: Very gentle local contact with the muscles just below the base of the skull.
